questions.title: Why was the Board’s narrowing of DuPont factor six treated as a legal error rather than a factual one?
questions.question_body: The opinion says legal conclusions are reviewed de novo and factual findings for substantial evidence. Likelihood of confusion is a legal question with factual underpinnings. Here, the Federal Circuit affirmed the Board’s factor-two factual finding (services are highly similar) but vacated factor six because the Board considered only third-party marks for credit card services and excluded other banking/financing uses. Is the mistake characterized as legal because it applied the wrong legal standard for 'similar goods' under factor six, even though the underlying evidence was factual? How do courts decide when an error in the DuPont framework is legal (scope/standard) versus factual (weight of evidence)?

questions.title: Under DuPont factor six, must the TTAB consider third-party "Aspire" marks used for broader banking/financing services, not just credit cards?
questions.question_body: The Board defined the relevant public for factor six as consumers of 'credit card services' and treated other uses of Aspire for banking/financing as 'essentially irrelevant.' The Federal Circuit said that was too narrow, especially since factor two had already found the parties’ services 'highly similar' and even 'legally identical, in part.' Is there a rule that the 'similarity' scope used under factor two should carry over to factor six? In practice, how broadly should 'similar goods and services' be drawn in financial services when the identifications include 'banking and financing services' on one side and 'credit card services' on the other?

questions.title: How many third-party uses are enough to show a mark is weak, and do registrations without proof of use count?
questions.question_body: The Board found nine Aspire-formative uses for credit card services and deemed that insufficient to show commercial weakness, contrasting cases like Juice Generation (26 third-party marks) and Jack Wolfskin (voluminous evidence). Is there any quantitative benchmark for 'considerable' or 'ubiquitous' third-party use, or is it context dependent? Also, does the evidence have to show actual marketplace use, or can third-party registrations alone meaningfully weaken a mark? On remand, if the TTAB includes broader banking/financing uses, what quality and type of third-party evidence typically moves the needle from 'normal' to 'weak' commercial strength?

questions.title: How can the TTAB define 'credit card services' after the ID Manual entry was deleted, and what sources govern interpreting legacy identifications?
questions.question_body: The Board noted that 'credit card services' was deleted from the Trademark ID Manual after CC Serve’s 1998 registration, then relied on dictionary definitions to construe the scope of 'credit card services' (issuing cards, processing payments, authorization, monitoring, account management, etc.). What is the legal basis for construing identification language when the ID Manual entry no longer exists or has changed—does the TTAB look to ordinary meaning at the time of registration, current ordinary meaning, the TMEP, or other interpretive sources? Are there precedents on interpreting legacy identifications when official taxonomy has shifted?

questions.title: Does adding the word 'BANK' to ASPIRE materially change the commercial impression for the first DuPont factor?
questions.question_body: Apex’s marks are ASPIRE BANK (word and design) versus CC Serve’s ASPIRE. The first DuPont factor analysis was vacated because the sixth factor could affect assessments of commercial strength and overall impression. Independently of strength, how much weight does the addition of a descriptive or generic term like 'BANK' typically carry in comparing marks? Would the presence of 'BANK' be discounted as merely descriptive of services, or could it meaningfully alter appearance, sound, connotation, or commercial impression in the financial-services context?

questions.title: On remand, can the TTAB reopen the record to accept new evidence on third-party use and commercial strength?
questions.question_body: The Federal Circuit vacated the TTAB’s findings on DuPont factors six and one and remanded for reconsideration. Is the Board limited to the evidentiary record as it stood, or may it accept additional evidence (e.g., more third-party uses or marketplace context) on remand in an inter partes opposition? What rules govern reopening the record after a Federal Circuit remand in a Section 2(d) case, and does the nature of the identified legal error (scope of similarity) affect whether new evidence is permitted or required?

questions.title: Why were costs awarded to the appellant despite only a partial victory (affirmed in part, vacated in part)?
questions.question_body: The judgment states 'Costs to appellant' even though the Federal Circuit affirmed the Board on DuPont factor two and only vacated and remanded on factors six and one. Under Federal Rule of Appellate Procedure 39 and the Federal Circuit’s local rules, how are costs allocated in a mixed outcome like this? Does obtaining a vacatur and remand on key issues generally make the appellant the 'prevailing party' for cost purposes, or is this a discretionary call the panel makes case by case?

questions.title: Why did the Board treat Apex’s broad 'banking and financing services' as encompassing credit card issuance even though Apex doesn’t currently issue cards?
questions.question_body: Apex argued the parties’ services aren’t directly competitive, emphasizing it doesn’t offer credit cards. The Board still found the services 'legally identical, in part' based on dictionary definitions of 'banking' and 'finance' that include extending credit via credit cards. In Section 2(d) oppositions, is the similarity of services assessed strictly by the identifications in the application/registration rather than actual marketplace activities? How do tribunals handle broad service identifications that logically subsume more specific services the applicant does not (yet) offer?
